title: Year with Maximum Population
statement:
You are given the life spans of `n` people. Person `i` is born at the start of year `birth[i]` and dies at the start of year `death[i]`, so they count as alive in every year `y` with `birth[i] ≤ y < death[i]` (in their death year they are no longer counted).

The **population** of a year is the number of people alive in it. Find the year with the greatest population. If several years share the greatest population, choose the **earliest** one.

Print that year and its population.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `birth[i]` and `death[i]`.
outputFormat: Print two space-separated integers: the earliest year with the maximum population, and that population.

examples.explanation: In year 5 the first and third people are alive (the third dies at the start of year 6), so the population is 2. In year 10 the first person is gone and only the second is alive. No year has 3 people, and year 5 is the earliest year with 2.
Year 1 has 1 person. Year 2 has persons 0 and 1, so the population is 2. Year 3 also has 2 and so does year 4, but year 2 is the earliest.

hints: The population only changes in a year where someone is born or someone dies, so you never need to look at the other years.
Record +1 at each birth year and -1 at each death year, then sweep the distinct event years in increasing order keeping a running total.
Because death years are exclusive, the -1 at a year applies from that year on. Only update the best answer when the running total is strictly larger, so the earliest year wins ties.
